newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean poverty fell sharply over decade - study.
newsitem.headline: Chilean poverty fell sharply over decade - study.

text.p: The percentage of people living in poverty in Chile has fallen by nearly half over the last decade, but there has been little improvement in income distribution, a government report said on Tuesday.
The study by the Planning Ministry showed the percentage of Chileans classed as poor fell to 23 percent of the total population last year from 45 percent in 1987.
The percentage of Chileans living in extreme poverty dropped to 5.8 percent of the population from 17 percent 10 years ago, the report said.
Out of Chile's population of nearly 14 million, 3.3 million people earn barely enough to support their basic needs, while 800,000 live in extreme poverty.
Despite the country's economic boom over the last decade, the survey showed wealth remained concentrated in the hands of few Chileans, with no improvement in income distribution in recent years.
"At the end of 1996, the distribution of income in the country remained highly concentrated," Planning Minister Roberto Pizarro said at the presentation of the report.
"If you compare the situation at the end of 1996 with previous years, it is clear that the distribution of monetary income has stayed practically unaltered," he said.
The report showed that the wealthiest 10 percent of Chileans earned 41 percent of national income in 1996, while the poorest 10 percent received just 1.4 percent.
The survey, which covered 33,000 homes throughout Chile in November and December, calculated poverty levels from the cost of a basket of food and of other necessities, including housing.
It estimated that an urban family of five needed $206 a month for food and a total monthly income of $412 to cover all its basic needs.
